title: Order XXXVII recovery plus a 2024 arbitration clause — Commercial Court, Jaipur

input.text: I am an advocate of intermediate standing at the Commercial Court, Jaipur. Plaintiff M/s Rajasthan Agro Supplies Pvt. Ltd. vs my client M/s Udaipur Agro Traders. Recovery of about ₹48.70 lakh under Order XXXVII CPC on unpaid invoices 2023–2025. Plaint 03.09.2026, appearance and leave to defend already taken, plaintiff has filed replication. Client: several invoices unsigned by any authorised partner; Dealership Agreement 15.03.2024 Clause 18 arbitration; some invoices look more than three years old. I need a paragraph-wise written statement, a Section 8 application, limitation matrix, COURT_SAFE commercial-bench citations only, English + Hindi. Next date approaching.

IN THE COURT OF THE COMMERCIAL JUDGE, JAIPUR
Suit No. ____ of 2026
M/s Rajasthan Agro Supplies Pvt. Ltd.  ... Plaintiff
v.
M/s Udaipur Agro Traders  ... Defendant

WRITTEN STATEMENT ON BEHALF OF THE DEFENDANT (review skeleton)

PRELIMINARY
1. The suit is for recovery of about ₹48.70 lakh on unpaid invoices 2023–2025 under Order XXXVII CPC (CPC 1908, Order XXXVII). Leave to defend was granted vide order dated [PENDING — leave-to-defend order date]; appearance and leave are already taken. This WS does not re-argue the summons.

PARA-WISE SPECIFIC DENIALS (CPC 1908, Order 8 rules 3–5 — specific, not general)
2. Para 1 of the plaint: [PENDING — reproduce each plaint paragraph and deny it specifically].
3. The invoices relied on are unsigned by any authorised partner of the Defendant; each invoice is separately denied, invoice-wise, in the limitation matrix.

ARBITRATION BAR
4. The Dealership Agreement dated 15.03.2024 contains Clause 18 (arbitration). Whether it covers invoice disputes is [UNCONFIRMED] — Clause 18 must be quoted from the agreement, not from the client's summary. If covered, the plaintiff is to be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, s. 8. Any commercial-bench holding on s. 8 vs civil suit is [PENDING — no named holding in this fixture].
5. No decision is cited from memory. The plea is kept bare, without a named case.

PRAYER
6. Dismiss the suit with costs; alternatively refer the parties to arbitration. [PENDING — supervised review before signature.]

teachingNotes: A general denial in a commercial written statement is a gift to the plaintiff.
Section 8 is lost by filing a merits-heavy WS first and the application later.
Limitation is pleaded invoice-wise or it is not pleaded.
commonMistakes: Copy-pasting a 'standard WS' with 'contents of para 1 are wrong' for every paragraph.
Citing a remembered commercial-bench case without a COURT_SAFE tag.
Forgetting Hindi for the partners and English for the court as two audiences, not two truths.
seniorVariants: Open with the arbitration bar, then limitation, then unsigned invoices.
Annex the agreement as the first exhibit of the s. 8 application, not of the WS.
If leave was conditional, check whether the condition has been complied with before attacking the plaint.

accuracy.adverseFact: If Clause 18 is a 'management dispute' clause and not a supplies clause, the entire s. 8 strategy fails and a late application may be treated as the first statement on merits.
